foreign_currency_exposure: HPE transacts in approximately 40 currencies; most significant for fiscal 2025 were the euro, Japanese yen, and British pound. For most currencies HPE is a net receiver of foreign currency.
fx_sensitivity_analysis: A hypothetical 10% adverse movement in foreign currency exchange rates would result in a foreign exchange fair value loss of 53 million at October 31, 2025 (44 million at October 31, 2024).
interest_rate_sensitivity_analysis: A hypothetical 10% adverse movement in interest rates would result in a loss in fair values of debt, debt investments and net portfolio assets, net of interest rate swaps, of 261 million at October 31, 2025 (233 million at October 31, 2024).
hedge_designation_types: Cash flow hedges (FX forwards/options protecting forecasted revenue and costs), net investment hedges (FX forwards hedging net investments in foreign subsidiaries), and fair value hedges (interest rate swaps on fixed-rate debt). Non-designated FX forwards for balance sheet exposure hedging.
underlying_exposures: Forecasted net revenue, cost of sales, operating expenses, intercompany loans denominated in non-USD currencies; fixed-rate debt subject to interest rate risk; balance sheet monetary assets/liabilities in foreign currencies.
debt_hedging_strategy: HPE uses interest rate swaps to modify market risk on debt, swapping fixed for floating or floating for fixed. When debt is denominated in foreign currency, HPE may use cross-currency swaps to exchange foreign currency principal and interest for USD-denominated amounts.
